meta.workDescription: The 633d Logistics Readiness Squadron Ground Transportation element at Joint Base Langley-Eustis serves as the primary logistics hub for the 1st Fighter Wing’s F-22 Raptor mission and Headquarters Air Combat Command. Personnel manage a versatile fleet ranging from general-purpose passenger vehicles and distinguished visitor transport to heavy tractor-trailers, wreckers, and forklifts. A primary operational focus is Documented Cargo Operations (DCO), where Airmen conduct specialized airfield operations to facilitate the time-definite delivery of mission-critical supplies and aircraft components directly to flight line maintenance units. By synchronizing vehicle recovery, deployment distributions, and joint-service logistics with high-visibility personnel movement, this work center ensures the seamless flow of resources necessary for installation sustainment and global power projection

selectedModules.title: Hazard Communication
selectedModules.reference: AFI 90-821 - Hazard Communication (HAZCOM) Program; 29 CFR 1910.1200 - Hazard Communication
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Provide effective training at initial assignment and whenever a new chemical hazard is introduced. Cover where hazardous chemicals are present, the written program, labels and SDS access, how releases are detected, hazard types, protective measures, emergency procedures, and required PPE.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.1200 - Hazard Communication
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Employees potentially exposed to chemical hazards must complete HAZCOM training upon initial assignment and whenever a new hazard or chemical is introduced or new tasks create new hazards. Supervisors must ensure SDS access for chemicals used in the work process.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 28.2.5 and para. 28.3.3

selectedModules.title: Forklift / Material Handling Equipment
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 35; 29 CFR 1910.178 - Powered industrial trucks
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Ensure each operator is trained and evaluated before operating independently. Training must combine formal instruction, practical training, and workplace evaluation, cover truck-specific and site-specific hazards, and include refresher training after unsafe operation, incidents, assignment to a different truck, or workplace changes.
selectedModules.trainingSource: OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards / 29 CFR 1910.178 - Powered industrial trucks
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: MHE training must follow equipment-specific lesson plans with formal instruction, hands-on demonstrations, exercises, and evaluation. Around aircraft, only licensed drivers will operate forklifts and hi-lift trucks, special training is required for hi-lift operators, and spotters must be used when maneuvering close to aircraft or raising and lowering cargo beds.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 12.6.1 through 12.6.5 and para. 24.13.10
selectedModules.notes:
Training provided through TVO IAW AFQTP 24-3-E814
Refresher Training will be conducted annual and documented in the RHINO Tracker.

selectedModules.title: Explosives Safety Training
selectedModules.reference: DESR 6055.09_DAFMAN 91-201 - Explosives Safety Standards; DAFI 91-202 - The Department of the Air Force (DAF) Mishap Prevention Program
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use explosives-specific AF lesson plans and local operating instructions. OSHA 2254 includes transportation and explosives references, but the Air Force explosives program should remain the primary training basis for this module.
selectedModules.trainingSource: DESR 6055.09_DAFMAN 91-201 - Explosives Safety Standards / local procedures
selectedModules.notes:
Initial training for explosives/hazardous material transport includes the educational and hands-on training, provided by AFQTP24-3-HAZMAT, and the successful completion of required computer-based training and the Performance Test.
Refresher training will be accomplished, biennially. Refresher training includes member completion of the required CBT training and the Performance Test.​
Explosives, to be acceptable for transportation by any mode, must have an assigned hazard classification (HD; storage CG; DOT class, markings, shipping name and label; and United Nations serial number)​

selectedModules.title: Flight Line Driving
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards Chapter 24
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use flight-line-specific AF lesson plans and local airfield driving rules. OSHA 2254 does not provide a direct flight-line driving training excerpt for this module.
selectedModules.trainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards / local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Use Chapter 24 flightline vehicle operations rules and local licensing programs. For specialized equipment like forklifts and hi-lifts around aircraft, only licensed drivers may operate and the owning organization must provide special training with spotter support as required.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 24.13 and para. 24.13.10
selectedModules.notes:
Supervisors or VCOs shall review individuals AF Form 110, Individual Incident Reference Record, and AF Form 1313, Driving Record, (located at Security Forces) to determine their qualifications, before permitting them to operate vehicles and (or) equipment on the flight line. ​
Upon completion of training, individuals will be issued an AF Form 483, Certificate of Competency, endorsed for flight line driving. ​
Refresher Training will be conducted annually.

selectedModules.title: Fetal Protection Program
selectedModules.reference: DAFMAN 48-146 - Occupational Health Program Management; AFRCI 41-104 - Professional Board and National Certification Examinations as applicable
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use AF occupational and public health guidance to brief reproductive hazards, reporting expectations, and referral procedures. No direct OSHA 2254 module is mapped here.
selectedModules.trainingSource: DAFMAN 48-146 - Occupational Health Program Management / local procedures
selectedModules.notes:
Fetal Protection Program Briefing. Supervisors have a big responsibility to ensure all females within their duty section receive appropriate health care as soon as possible when they suspect a pregnancy. Ensure all females in the duty section who become pregnant report to Public Health to receive a Fetal Protection Briefing. This briefing must then be recorded on the AF Form 55 or an equivalent product. See AFI 48-145 for further information/guidance.​
Immediately report confirmed pregnancy to workplace supervisor and Medical. 
​

selectedModules.title: Jewelry / Loose Articles Restrictions
selectedModules.reference: Workplace-specific limits on rings, necklaces, watches, and loose items
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Use local shop rules and hazard analysis to define where jewelry, loose clothing, or unsecured items are prohibited around moving parts, climbing, electrical work, or snag hazards.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
selectedModules.notes: Jewelry, such as rings, watches, bracelets and necklaces, are not permitted for wear during the inspection and servicing of vehicles nor during the securement of cargo along with warehouse work.

selectedModules.title: Manual Lifting and Material Handling
selectedModules.reference: Manual lifting techniques and available lifting devices
selectedModules.trainingRequirement: Cover shop-specific lifting limits, two-person lift triggers, hand truck and lifting-device use, and when supervisors require assisted handling. No direct OSHA 2254 standalone manual-lifting module is mapped here.
selectedModules.trainingSource: No direct OSHA 2254 - Training Requirements in OSHA Standards training excerpt; local procedures
selectedModules.afTrainingRequirement: Supervisors must ensure thorough training on proper manual lifting techniques, required PPE, and the use of manual lifting devices. Training must use both verbal and written materials, include practice on proper motions, and be documented under DAFI 91-202.
selectedModules.afTrainingSource: DAFMAN 91-203 - Air Force Occupational Safety, Fire and Health Standards para. 2.10.3
selectedModules.notes:
Personnel will be instructed in proper handling techniques for the equipment and materials received.​
Supervisors will evaluate personnel on a periodic basis and correct improper techniques when necessary.
